directions: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in average to lean, well-drained soil in full sun; Blue Mist is an older, long-cultivated selection valued for its soft, powder-blue flowers, a notably paler and more pastel shade than the deep violet-blue of Dark Knight or Longwood Blue. Aromatic gray-green foliage covers a compact, rounded mound that dies back to the ground in cold winters and resprouts vigorously from the base each spring. From late summer into fall the stems are wreathed in dense clusters of small, fringed flowers that draw bees and butterflies at a time when few other shrubs are still blooming, making it a dependable late-season nectar source for pollinators. Cut the whole plant back to a few inches from the ground in late winter, since it flowers on new wood and benefits from hard annual pruning to stay compact and floriferous.

The chartreuse-gold leaves create a luminous backdrop for the clusters of cobalt-blue, fringed flowers that appear from late summer into fall, giving strong two-tone contrast in a sunny border. Like other caryopteris, it dies back to the ground in cold winters and resprouts from the base each spring, and its late, nectar-rich blooms are heavily visited by bees and butterflies when few other shrubs are still flowering. Cut the whole plant back to a few inches from the ground in late winter, since it flowers on new wood and benefits from hard annual pruning to stay compact and floriferous.

Its compact, tidy habit fits neatly into a smaller sunny border or foundation planting, and like other caryopteris it dies back to the ground in cold winters, resprouting vigorously from the base each spring. The richly colored, fringed flowers wreathe the upper stems from late summer into fall and are a magnet for bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds at a time when few other shrubs are still in bloom. Cut the whole plant back to a few inches from the ground in late winter, since it flowers on new wood and benefits from hard annual pruning to stay compact and floriferous.
